articles.title: ICE’s new ‘shock gloves’ are dangerous, inhumane and totally unnecessary
articles.summary: A rogue agency that violates human and civil rights does not deserve more weapons.
articles.body:
According to a recent Department of Homeland Security notice, the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency plans to spend up to $20 million on gloves that deliver painful electric shocks. At the push of a button, a one-second shock from these gloves can send a grown man to the ground.

On “Fox & Friends,” White House border czar Tom Homan said the gloves would prevent ICE agents from needing to use deadly force. “It’s another device to help someone get compliant when they are not.”

These shock gloves are a new low in ICE’s campaign of cruelty. Their use holds great potential for harm to migrants and U.S. citizens alike, and will enable more ICE brutality while helping agents evade accountability for their actions.

The manufacturer of the gloves, formally named the Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter, markets them as a “de-escalation device.” But there is no reason to believe that ICE agents will use them that way. Instead, the gloves will likely embolden a paramilitary force known for aggressive behavior, racial profiling and violence.

ICE agents have kicked, punched and tackled people hundreds of times, and deployed chemical irritants regularly. They use chokeholds and neck restraints, tactics that are prohibited by other law enforcement agencies. They have fatally shot at least three confirmed American citizens: Alex Pretti, Renee Good and Ruben Ray Martinez. With the shock gloves, agents will have a new tool with which to inflict pain on anyone they say is suspected of being in the country illegally.

The manufacturer of the shock gloves warns that they should not be used on children, pregnant woman, the elderly or disabled people. Yet ICE frequently encounters members of these high-risk categories. People with disabilities are especially vulnerable to harm from the gloves, because not all medical conditions — like epilepsy, heart disease or mental health issues — are visible. Given that ICE disproportionately targets Latinos , a demographic with high rates of cardiovascular disease, the planned use of the gloves will almost certainly lead to serious medical incidents.

Consider that the gloves’ training manual comes with a red warning label , noting that improper use may result in injury or death.

The rationale behind the use of such gloves is disturbing. They were specifically designed to be “low optics,” meaning their use will not be visible as other policing methods. On a promotional video by the manufacturer, supporters of the gloves say that they “Look better to those witnesses” and that they are “conducive to not leading to lawsuits.” Because the electric shocks do not leave burns or marks, there is nothing to stop agents from using the gloves repeatedly on a person, or after a person has been subdued. Nor is there anything to prevent multiple agents from shocking a single person simultaneously. What could possibly go wrong?

The real question is why ICE needs these gloves at all. Immigration agents are well equipped with firearms, pepper spray and batons. ICE and the Customs and Border Protection agency plan to spend $144 million in 2025 on guns, ammunition and “less lethal” weapons such as tasers and pepper sprays, according to a February report by Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.). Just weeks later, the administration announced its intent to purchase more than 17,000 tasers for another $220 million . It’s hard to see how agents need another tool in their arsenal when they are already armed to the hilt.

ICE’s shock gloves raise legal issues as well. Their use may violate the Eighth Amendment’s prohibition of “cruel and unusual punishment,” and the constitutional guarantee of due process. New York’s governor and attorney general have both criticized the new gloves , suggesting that their use may run afoul of state and civil rights laws.

In a statement, the Department of Homeland Security said , “ICE is constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country.” Yet ICE is generally not going after “criminal illegal aliens.” About 70 percent of people in immigration detention have no criminal convictions at all. ICE is also operating in an environment with little oversight, as the administration has gutted the agency’s internal watchdogs .

Meanwhile, the president’s popularity is cratering , and a majority of American voters disapprove of how ICE is doing its job. Immigration agents should be reined in, not empowered to inflict more suffering on their targets.

ICE’s shock gloves are dangerous, inhumane and unnecessary. A rogue agency that violates human and civil rights does not deserve more weapons.

Raul A. Reyes is an award-winning journalist, attorney and television commentator in New York City.

articles.title: Former labor secretary created ‘toxic’ atmosphere, drank at work and misused funds, report says
articles.summary: Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated multiple department policies during her tenure, including creating a hostile work environment, using government funds for personal travel and having an inappropriate relationship with an employee, according to a department watchdog.
articles.body: Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated multiple department policies during her tenure, including creating a hostile work environment, using government funds for personal travel and having an inappropriate relationship with an employee, according to a department watchdog. The Labor Department inspector general’s 44-page report, released Thursday, is the culmination of an investigation that began in early January after an anonymous complaint alleging misconduct. The report also accuses other former top officials who worked with Chavez-DeRemer of multiple violations of department policy. More than three-dozen witnesses described working with Chavez-DeRemer, who led the department from March 2025 to April this year, as “toxic, intimidating and humiliating,” according to the report. The inspector general’s office, however, didn’t “determine whether the conduct described in the evidence above was sufficient to constitute unlawful discrimination, retaliation, or a hostile work environment” under federal law. The report touched on the previously reported inappropriate relationship that Chavez-DeRemer had with a member of her security detail. The inspector general said they “developed and maintained an inappropriately close and unprofessional relationship,” but that it “did not, however, obtain sufficient direct evidence to establish that the relationship was romantic or sexual.” In April 2025, the report said, Chavez-DeRemer requested an off-the-record stop during personal travel to Oregon at a place that featured “partially nude dancers” with the member of the protective detail with whom she had a relationship. The secretary asked another agent to take money from her purse and “drop the bills one by one onto the partially nude woman.” Some of the other policy violations that Chavez-DeRemer committed, according to the inspector general, included improperly combining personal and official travel, consuming and storing alcohol on federal property and accepting gifts without reporting them under ethics rules. The gifts included an alligator-hide wallet, work boots, baby gifts and cowboy hats, the report said. The inspector general also said that Chavez-DeRemer directed her employees to perform personal tasks for her, including going to her residence during work hours to organize her bedroom closet. Reached for comment, Chavez-DeRemer’s attorney, Nick Oberheiden, said in a statement, “Secretary Chavez-DeRemer did not violate any law. That’s important to point out and contrast to the premature and incorrect speculation of some. Beyond this, Ms. Chavez-DeRemer has successfully pursued new projects as a private citizen.” Chavez-DeRemer resigned in April amid the allegations of misconduct. At the time, Oberheiden said the decision was “not the result of legal wrongdoings. It is a personal decision.” The Labor Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the inspector general’s findings.

articles.title: Ty Cobb on midterms: Trump intends ‘to steal these elections where possible’
articles.summary: Former Trump White House lawyer Ty Cobb said Thursday that President Trump would attempt to “steal” the 2026 midterm elections “where possible.” Cobb, in an appearance on MS NOW, discussed reports of GOP lawmakers declining to attend a Republican National Committee event, underlining concerns about Trump’s political brand almost two years into his second term.…
articles.body:
Former Trump White House lawyer Ty Cobb said Thursday that President Trump would attempt to “steal” the 2026 midterm elections “where possible.”

Cobb, in an appearance on MS NOW, discussed reports of GOP lawmakers declining to attend a Republican National Committee event, underlining concerns about Trump’s political brand almost two years into his second term.

A source familiar told The Hill that the National Republican Congressional Committee distributed more than 2,000 tickets for the convention and that around 100 members and candidates were confirmed to attend. Lawmakers are expected to contribute a minimum of $25,000 to take part.

“Well, I think the Republicans who are saying no are being strategic,” Cobb said. “But at the same time, he’s [Trump] sitting on $400 million in campaign money that he could donate to some of these elections. And he’s not.”

Cobb added that, “It also plays into a narrative that I think people are undervaluing, which is I think Trump doesn’t feel he needs to spend this money because it is his intention to interfere with the elections and to steal these elections where possible.”

He raised the possibility that Trump could “urge” House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) to refuse to swear in Democratic candidates following the midterm elections. Johnson was an active backer of Trump’s efforts to overturn his 2020 election loss to former President Biden.

The Trump administration is still pushing to restrict mail-in voting for the midterms, even as states start sending out early ballots. The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to allow for the U.S. Postal Service’s implementation of Trump’s executive order targeting mail voting.

The Postal Service’s plan would mandate that states’ mail-in ballots meet design requirements — such as unique barcodes and an official logo — and require election officials to upload lists of voters who are eligible to vote by mail. If a ballot doesn’t meet the specifications or someone is not on the submitted list, the service would refuse to deliver it.

In a July appearance on MS NOW, Cobb argued that moves from Trump like this are rooted in his refusal to accept his 2020 defeat.

“The most grievous thing that ever happened to him was he lost an election,” he said at the time. “As a malignant narcissist, he just can’t abide that.”

articles.title: Former podcaster charged for death threats against Trump
articles.summary: Former podcaster Benjamin Azariah Southworth was charged Thursday in connection with death threats against President Trump. FBI Director Kash Patel announced Southworth was arrested in a statement on the social platform X, writing, “Early this morning, the @FBI and partners arrested Benjamin Azariah Southworth in LA – after a federal grand jury indicted him for…
articles.body:
Former podcaster Benjamin Azariah Southworth was charged Thursday in connection with death threats against President Trump.

FBI Director Kash Patel announced Southworth was arrested in a statement on the social platform X , writing, “Early this morning, the @FBI and partners arrested Benjamin Azariah Southworth in LA – after a federal grand jury indicted him for allegedly threatening to assassinate President Trump and his attorney, Jay Sekulow.”

“Deadly threats like this are as vile as they are criminal – those responsible will be met by this FBI and law enforcement,” Patel added.

The grand jury indictment found Southworth used his social media — including his Instagram, YouTube and Tiktok — to “publicly engage in and/or encourage the abuse, harassment and intimidation of, and violence against, President Trump.”

The second victim was not identified in the indictment but was described as “President Trump’s personal lawyer and that lawyer’s family.”

Southworth is the former host of the podcast “Yass, Jesus!” and a Christian reality show called “The Remix.”

Prosecutors cited as evidence a video Southworth posted in April where he reportedly made death threats against the president and portrayed “fictitious portrayals of acts of violence” against Trump.

Southworth allegedly posted in April on his social platforms, “IF AT FIRST YOU FAIL, TRY AGAIN!” following a shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.

Three months before these posts, prosecutors said Southworth also posted Jay Sekulow’s home address along with his picture on his personal TikTok account with a statement that read, “No peace for traitors.”

He is charged with cyberstalking and harassing Sekulow and threatening to kill Trump.

“As threats against President Trump’s life escalate, the Department of Justice will respond with the full force of the law,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a press release . “We will hold perpetrators of violent threats accountable, and anyone who makes these threats online will not be allowed to hide behind their screens.”

The case is still under investigation. If convicted, Southworth would face a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison for threatening the president, a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison for cyberstalking and a statutory maximum sentence of two years in federal prison for telephonic harassment.

articles.title: The war on women is happening in a warehouse, not in the statehouse
articles.summary: Policy decisions that deeply affect millions of working women will be finalized this November.
articles.body:
The next front in the fight for the rights of American women is not in the doctor’s office. It’s in an Amazon fulfillment warehouse and a Speedway convenience store. That’s where working-class women in shift and hourly jobs, the backbone of the American economy, suffer systematic abuses that may get worse pending the results of this year’s midterm elections.

That’s because policy decisions that deeply affect millions of working women will be finalized this November as American voters cast ballots grading President Trump’s second term.

The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, an under-the-radar government agency created decades ago to protect women and minorities against unfair workplace measures, is being hollowed out from within as, in the administration’s words, a place for white men to report perceived abuses.

The commission announced late last month that it will finalize new proposed policy regulations within days of the elections, including undoing decades of workplace policy advances that allowed women to balance work and family.

Among other destructive line items, it is anticipated that new policy measures will essentially negate the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act , a bipartisan law signed in 2022 that ensured basic workplace accommodations for pregnant and postpartum women. These accommodations are often remarkably modest: access to water, temporary lifting restrictions, bathroom breaks, a chair during the third trimester, time off for prenatal treatments or fertility procedures or space to pump breast milk.

But unmaking these measures will result in systematically pushing women out of the workplace. And that’s exactly what they are intended to do, whether it is freshly emboldened, multibillion-dollar mega-corporations seeking to automate or fringe religious activists long eager to turn back the clock on women exiting the home to endter the workforce.

The women most affected are not executives or professionals with college degrees and jobs with typically generous leave and accommodations policies. The women most affected will be warehouse pickers, cashiers and factory workers who cannot work from home or absorb months without a paycheck, who desperately depend on their $20 per hour wages.

Consider the story of an Amazon warehouse associate with a high-risk pregnancy who reached out to my organization. Despite doctors’ orders, Amazon refused her basic accommodations, including sitting breaks. She was repeatedly hospitalized before ultimately losing her job.

A pregnant Speedway cashier who reached out to us was likewise denied the ability to sit while working. She suffered a pregnancy-related medical emergency and was forced onto involuntary, unpaid leave.

These changes at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission are not occurring in isolation. They fit within a broader agenda that increasingly seeks to push women toward motherhood and away from economic independence. Trump has considered numerous such proposals — including birthing bonuses and even a “ national medal of motherhood ” for women with six or more children.

It is not just a regressive concept of societal roles. Passing the SAVE Act would also make it more difficult for millions of women to vote, and the Department of Health and Human Services is undermining comprehensive reproductive health care and advancing a narrow vision of women’s health centered on childbirth.

Few of these developments have entered the national conversation, which is likely by design. The affected women are largely working-class and fearful of losing a paycheck. They cannot afford legal teams, lobbyists and communications specialists.

My organization’s free legal helpline hears from thousands of workers each year with similar stories. Their pleas are not political, but practical. Can they keep their jobs while pregnant? Can they return to work after having a baby? Can they continue supporting their families without being forced to choose between their health and their paycheck?

These questions go to the heart of whether the nation’s economy can include women, and whether the concept of opportunity means anything at all if women can be pushed out of the workforce because it serves a radical political ideology.

In four months, millions of Americans will head to the polls. The same month, a federal agency will take a massive step toward allowing the firing of millions of American women, permanently altering the independence of women across the country.

If there is no accountability for this incoming economic and social disaster, it will be because we let it happen. And, in doing so, we would reveal that the women who pack our deliveries and swipe our cards after we fill up the car just aren’t very important to some people.

Inimai Chettiar is the president of A Better Balance, an advocate for paid leave, family leave and workplace policy advancements for women and families.

articles.title: Farage announces ‘entente cordiale’ between Reform and National Rally
articles.summary: Nigel Farage announced a “new entente cordiale” with France’s right-wing National Rally party as he pledged to work together to stop small boats crossing the...
articles.body:
Nigel Farage announced a new partnership with France's National Rally party to work together on stopping small boats crossing the Channel.

The deal signed by Farage and National Rally President Jordan Bardella commits the two parties to cooperate on returning migrants to France, with both parties hoping to win their next national elections.

France and the UK already have a £501-million deal in place to stop launches from the French coast, with Channel crossings down 40% compared to last year, but thousands of migrants are still arriving.

Nigel Farage announced a "new entente cordiale" with France's right-wing National Rally party as he pledged to work together to stop small boats crossing the Channel.

The deal, signed by Farage and National Rally President Jordan Bardella at the Reform conference on Friday, commits the two parties to co-operate on returning migrants to France.

The Reform UK leader referenced the early 20th century treaties between the UK and France to signify the close relations between his party and Bardella's if both win their next national elections.

France is due to hold its next presidential election in April. National Rally has led in polling since March last year.

Bardella's predecessor, Marine le Pen, is due to be the party's candidate for president of France. She previously led the National Front party.

Farage told the Reform conference: "We today are going to begin a genuine new entente cordiale between our parties and our countries."

He added: "We are about to sign a memorandum of understanding between our two parties, and we hope and believe our next two governments, where we reaffirm our commitment to stopping illegal immigration, where France say they'll do their utmost to stop all departures and maybe this time, with him as prime minister, they will actually mean it."

Addressing the event in English, Bardella said: "The great challenge is one we all know; taking back control of immigration. In recent years, [French President] Emmanuel Macron has failed to protect our country.

"For him mass migration is not a problem, it's a project. France must now regain the trust of its own people, but also the trust of its neighbours and partners. France must take back control, and France must finally keep its word.

"Dear friends here in Birmingham, I make you this promise. If the French people bring us to power in 2027 in a few months, with the Rassemblement National [National Rally] and Marine le Pen, our government will do everything in its power to ensure that France is no longer the gateway for illegal migration into the United Kingdom."

France and the UK already have a £501-million ($677-million) deal in place, signed by Keir Starmer's government in April, designed to stop launches from the French coast.

Channel crossings are down 40% compared to last year. The number of crossings this summer are at their lowest level since 2019. However, thousands are still arriving – with larger boats being used to transport migrants over the summer.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Macron discussed the issue during the latter's visit on Thursday. A boost in the number of police officers tackling "mega-dinghies" was announced in advance.

Bardella told the Reform conference: "The destination of illegal migrants entering France should not be the United Kingdom, they should be returned to their countries of origin."

He continued: "We must put an end to these deadly routes, we must break the smuggler business model and together we must take control of our borders.

"If we win the election, our government's immigration policy will be simple. You do not enter France simply because you have decided to. You enter France because France has allowed you to.

"We will restore control and protection at our borders and we will send foreign criminals back to their countries."

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial ends in hung jury, defense demands stay of mistrial declaration
articles.summary: The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case announced Friday he was declaring a mistrial after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict. However, when defense attorney Kevin Reddington requested an immediate stay of the declaration, the judge gave the defense one hour to appeal.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) – The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case announced Friday that he was declaring a mistrial after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict. However, when defense attorney Kevin Reddington requested an immediate stay of the declaration, the judge gave the defense one hour to appeal.

The jury, composed of nine women and three men, had deliberated for seven days after five weeks of testimony. The jury told the judge by note Friday, “It is with a heavy heart we are still unable to come to a decision and will not be able to.”

In the case of a mistrial, prosecutors have the option of retrying in front of a different jury in a new trial, but they aren’t required to do so. Prosecutors can decide whether to try Clancy again, pursue a plea deal or drop the charges.

The jury informed the judge that they were deadlocked twice this week and were sent back to continue deliberations each time.

Earlier Friday, Judge William Sullivan decided not to remove a holdout juror after Reddington said the juror should be booted for refusing to follow instructions on reasonable doubt, “whether they like it or not.”

He instead said the jury would again be reminded of their duties, stating he had read them the instructions on how to come to a decision beyond “reasonable doubt.”

Reddington called Sullivan’s reading of those jury instructions “soft,” and asked the judge to do it more “forcefully.”

“What do you want me to do? Get a brass band?” Sullivan said in the heated exchange.

In Thursday’s proceedings, a note was sent to Sullivan in the trial, indicating 11 of the 12 jurors had decided on a verdict, with only one juror holding out, according to Reddington.

On Wednesday, after two days in a deadlock, Judge Sullivan read jurors the Tuey-Rodriguez instruction, also known as a “ dynamite charge ,” a Massachusetts law that instructs jurors to assess their own views and those opposing without dismissing their own honestly held beliefs.

State law says a judge cannot send the jury back to deliberate a third time without their consent, unless they ask the court for further explanation of the law.

The jury has spent more than six days and over 35 hours deliberating. The prosecution argued Clancy knew what she was doing when she killed her three kids in 2023. The defense argued she was in the grip of postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible.

Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) announced Thursday he would broaden his probe into Flock Safety’s roadside cameras to include AI surveillance networks run by three other companies. “Flock does not stand alone in the surveillance industry,” wrote the senator, who chairs the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, on social media. “Other companies are also…
articles.body:
Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) announced Thursday he would broaden his probe into Flock Safety’s roadside cameras to include AI surveillance networks run by three other companies.

“Flock does not stand alone in the surveillance industry,” wrote the senator, who chairs the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, on social media .

“Other companies are also building large camera networks, assisted by artificial intelligence, that intrude on the privacy of all Americans,” he continued. “That is why I’m expanding my investigation.”

In new letters to the top executives of Motorola Solutions Inc. , Verkada Inc. and Axon Enterprise Inc. , Hawley requested information about these companies’ policies around the retention and use of citizen data collected by their AI camera networks.

The Hill has reached out to all three companies for comment.

Last week, the Missouri lawmaker wrote to Flock CEO Garrett Langley, expressing concerns that the company’s network of more than 120,000 cameras across 49 states has led to “abuse and misuse of personal data” because of a “woeful lack of safeguards in these systems.”

The company has faced public outcry amid reports that police officers across the nation have abused the nationwide surveillance network to spy on former romantic partners. Several police departments have severed their contracts with the company due to concerns about a lack of safeguards.

GOP Rep. Thomas Massie (Ky.) unveiled the Flock-Off Act in the House this week, which would block the use of federal funding for automated license plate reader cameras and biometric surveillance cameras.

“The federal government shouldn’t provide ‘security’ grants to cities and police departments that have gone beyond the pale and turned their communities into a version of ‘1984,’” the Kentucky Republican said in a press release.

Flock criticized the House bill in a statement to The Hill on Thursday, warning it could “have real consequences for public safety.”

“Rather than banning a critical public safety tool, Congress should consider strong, clear safeguards that ensure accountability, oversight, and responsible use are enshrined in law,” a company spokesperson said. “We do not have to choose between protecting privacy and giving law enforcement the tools it needs to keep communities safe. We can — and should — do both.”

articles.title: Farage unveils small boats deal with French National Rally party
articles.summary: Reform says it would use the Navy to intercept boats and return migrants to France, if the party wins power.
articles.body:
Nigel Farage has agreed a deal with France's hard-right National Rally (RN) party on returning migrants who attempt to cross the English Channel in small boats, should both parties win power.

It comes after Reform UK last month announced a plan to intercept boats and return migrants to French ports using the Royal Navy.

The proposed agreement with RN states that France would "ordinarily accept" those on board, and then repatriate them to their home country.

It was signed at Reform's annual conference in Birmingham by RN President Jordan Bardella, whose party is currently leading in opinion polls ahead of presidential elections in April next year.

In a speech in the main conference hall, ahead of the deal being unveiled, Bardella told delegates that an RN government would "do everything in its power to ensure that France is no longer the gateway for illegal migration into the United Kingdom".

Hailing Farage as the UK's next prime minister, Bardella pledged to work with a potential future Reform government to tackle illegal migration.

The "memorandum of understanding" unveiled at the conference is a political document, but could be developed into a legal agreement between two future governments, if both parties win power.

It states: "The United Kingdom will intercept boats which have launched from French shores and entered British territorial waters and will return the persons on board to France.

"France will ordinarily accept these persons, who will be repatriated to their home country in accordance with the law in force in France concerning expulsion."

Under the proposals, illegal migrants who successfully arrive in the UK from France would be immediately detained and deported to their home country, rather than to France, under plans previously outlined by Reform .

Challenged during a news conference over whether the wording "ordinarily" meant some migrants would not be accepted by France, Farage said it was "legalese".

He argued the proposals would mean there was "no incentive" to pay a trafficker to cross the Channel, and "in very, very short order the business model is broken".

Farage said the "historic document" would "stop the boats forever".

Achieving this goal within the first 100 days of a Reform government is one of the party's key pledges.

Last month Emmanuel Macron's government hit out at Reform's proposals to use the Navy to return migrant boats to France, saying the they would violate the country's sovereignty and breach international law.

Opposition parties also branded the plan unworkable.

Labour has pointed to increased cooperation with France as contributing to the number of small boat crossings falling.

This includes extra officers being deployed to French beaches, and more funding to help prevent crossings.

Last year Sir Keir Starmer's government also signed a "one in, one out deal" , which allows the UK to send some small boat-arrivals back to France, while agreeing to take the same number of people from France believed to have a legitimate claim to come to the UK.

Joining Bardella on the stage after his speech, Farage said the deal marked a "new Entente Cordiale" between France and the UK, in reference to a series of agreements in 1904 that paved the way for greater diplomatic cooperation.

Unveiling the memorandum, the pair signed a large mock-up of the document to cheers from the audience of Reform members, with one shouting "Vive la France!".

Farage has been forging closer ties with Bardella and his party since meeting the politician in London last December.

Previously tipped as a potential candidate for the 2027 presidential election, Le Pen has said she wants to make Bardella prime minister if RN wins power.

It comes after party leader Le Pen announced in July she would run for the presidency following a Paris appeal court ruling which upheld her conviction for misusing EU funds but shortened her sentence, clearing the path for her to stand.

articles.title: Fetterman stood up disabled veterans; scoffed at children’s hospital’s concerns: Report
articles.summary: Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) reportedly cancelled a meeting with three disabled veterans almost a year after he dismissed concerns about funding concerns for a children’s hospital. The Wall Street Journal published a report Wednesday that alleged the first-term Senator faked an illness to avoid meeting with the veterans, later opting to do an interview with…
articles.body:
Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) reportedly cancelled a meeting with three disabled veterans almost a year after he dismissed concerns about funding concerns for a children’s hospital.

The Wall Street Journal published a report Wednesday that alleged the first-term Senator faked an illness to avoid meeting with the veterans, later opting to do an interview with Fox News on Israel and the war in Iran in seemingly good health.

Fetterman – who reportedly went for almost a year without participating in a public event in Pennsylvania – tried to also dodge a meeting with the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP).

In 2025 messages with an aide, Fetterman questioned continual meetings with CHOP, writing, “Why do I have to keep having to meet with CHOP?”

“Because they are worried about vaccines and Medicaid cuts,” the aide answered.

“Well I’m not,” Fetterman wrote. “I’m convinced they just want free trips to DC.”

A report from Public Citizen in March found that the One Big, Beautiful Bill Act package last year that cut Medicaid funding put more than 400 hospitals across the country in danger of closing or reducing services.

Fetterman at the time voted against the package which included Medicaid funding cuts, saying, “I’ll keep fighting to protect health care.”

Other alleged messages from 2025, appeared to show Fetterman backing out of a funeral for police officers who were killed in the Keystone State – citing the event’s length.

“Yes it’s a very formal ceremony and the equivalent of 3 separate funerals,” an aide wrote back.

“This may be a nonstarter,” Fetterman responded.

The three officers were killed in the line of duty while attempting to serve a warrant in North Codorus Township at the time – miles away from Fetterman’s hometown.

The WSJ report noted that for the past year, Fetterman attended 26 of the 31 full hearings for his assigned committees but did not speak in 20 of them.

Fetterman’s office did not respond to The Hill’s request for immediate comment on the report.

Pennsylvania Democrats have voiced outrage about the report, with Rep. Brendan Boyle (D-Pa.) calling Fetterman “a disgrace.”

“Our state deserves better than a lazy trust fund baby who is too lazy to do the job,” Boyle said on social platform X .

While the senator is not up for re-election in this midterm cycle, Rep. Chris Deluzio (D-Pa.) said on Thursday , “Pennsylvania will do something about it in 2028.”

articles.title: Republicans face a dilemma over Trump’s role in the midterms
articles.summary: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, both parties face significant challenges regarding presidential popularity and internal ideological divisions.
articles.body:
All 435 House seats, along with 35 seats in the Senate (including special elections in Florida and Ohio) , will be up for grabs in the midterm elections. President Trump’s name will not be on any of those ballots. Not a single one.

And yet just about every Democrat will be running against him.

Midterm elections are a report card on how the president is doing — and voters almost always decide the president, any president, isn’t doing a good enough job. That is why the president’s party almost always loses seats in Congress.

And as the midterms approach, this president’s report card doesn’t look very good . Most Americans give him low marks on just about everything. His approval numbers are under water on foreign policy, on healthcare, on immigration and on the economy, the single most important issue in this and most elections. And then there’s the war the president said would be over in a few weeks.

So 2026 isn’t exactly shaping up to be a banner year for the Republican Party.

But Democrats have problems of their own.

They like to say that theirs is a “big tent” party, one that welcomes candidates with all sorts of opinions and views. Fair enough. Except this year the tent has quite a few people in it whose views Americans probably won’t like — assuming Republicans are smart enough to tell voters what those views actually are.

It’s not exactly breaking news that the energy in the Democratic Party is on the left. Candidates espousing one version or another of socialism have won primary elections, and not only in deep-blue places like New York City.

Republicans will undoubtedly try to make the election about what the Democratic Party’s hard left believes — that America isn’t particularly exceptional, that much of its history is ugly and perhaps irredeemable, and that the country needs to be fundamentally changed.

Let’s just say it’s not exactly an upbeat message.

So the midterms may come down not to which candidates voters like more, but which side they detest less: the party that welcomes, however grudgingly, democratic socialists into their big tent along with their message that can sound like America needs a complete overhaul — or the party of Donald Trump, with all the chaos that implies.

Which brings me to another question: Are Republicans better off if Trump leaves the White House, hits the road, and campaigns for Republican candidates — or if he stays put in Washington, and to the extent he’s capable, doesn’t make waves?

The argument for sending him out on the road is obvious. He can rev up the Republican base and encourage Republican voters to turn out. Without him on the campaign trail, the thinking goes, some of those voters might just stay home. So he is constantly telling Republicans: “ Pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot .”

But there’s a problem. Trump doesn’t just rev up Republicans. Nobody energizes Democrats more than he does. The more Democrats see him on their local newscasts, the more likely they are to get angry — and angry voters have a funny habit of showing up on Election Day.

It’s true that Democrats don’t need much encouragement this year to get off the couch and vote, such is their fear and loathing of the president. But what about that crucial bloc of voters — independents? They often decide close elections — and they’re hardly charter members of the Trump fan club.

There’s another problem. When Trump headlines a political rally, you sometimes get the impression he has forgotten why he was there. He rambles from one subject to another, inevitably goes off script, and too often says something outrageous that becomes the news of the day.

And suddenly nobody is talking about the Republican candidate he supposedly came to help.

That’s the Trump paradox for Republicans: The man who may be best at getting their voters to the polls may also be the man best at getting everybody else there, too.

My vote? With only a few exceptions, I think the president should stay in Washington and — for a change — concentrate on what voters actually care about, like grocery and gas prices, instead of golden ballrooms and majestic arches.

If he shows up to support a Republican in a tight race, there’s a good chance swing voters will do what swing voters do: Swing the other way.

Sometimes the best campaign contribution a president can make is knowing when not to campaign.

Bernard Goldberg is an Emmy and an Alfred I. duPont-Columbia University award-winning writer and journalist. He is the author of five books and publishes exclusive weekly columns, audio commentaries and Q&As on his Substack page .

articles.title: Mamdani faces growing 9/11 backlash as old post resurfaces ahead of Ground Zero ceremony: 'Is this real?'
articles.summary: Zohran Mamdani faces backlash over a resurfaced 2023 post about 9/11 as critics and 9/11 families urge him not to attend Ground Zero's commemoration.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing renewed scrutiny after a 2023 post marking the 9/11 attacks resurfaced online, in which he referenced the deaths and suffering caused by wars that followed the attacks. "Nearly 3,000 New Yorkers died on 9/11; 22 years later, the death hasn't stopped. We mourn our neighbors who died that day. The hundreds of thousands who died in the wars that followed. The unknown millions injured & displaced. In their memory, we work toward a better world," Mamdani wrote on X in 2023. Some 9/11 families have called on the socialist mayor not to attend New York City’s 9/11 commemoration after he faced backlash for interviewing Hasan Piker, who in 2019 said, "America deserved 9/11." Mamdani initially declined to condemn the remarks but later called them "objectionable and reprehensible." Critics have accused Mamdani of using the solemn anniversary to draw attention to the wars that followed 9/11 while notably leaving out who carried out the attacks and describing the deaths in passive terms. NEW YORK GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE URGES 9/11 ATTENDEES TO TURN AWAY FROM MAMDANI DURING CEREMONY "As someone who was in the Pentagon when the planes hit, this is absolutely disgraceful. You have no business ever setting foot at Ground Zero, much less on 9/11. If you dare show up, I hope you are greeted with such a Bronx cheer that you slink away in shame," wrote Marc Thiessen. "I guess they all just 'died' in an accident? And then you wonder why the families of 9/11 victims don’t want you at the ceremony. Stay home, Mamdani," wrote New York City council woman Inna Vernikov. "Nearly 25 years later, NYC’s Mayor is in bed with Muslim terrorists and refuses to call out evil for what it is. Unfortunately, it seems the city forgot when they elected Jihadi Mamdani mayor. But we never will," wrote Florida Rep. Randy Fine. RETIRED PORT AUTHORITY OFFICERS TELL MAMDANI, HOCHUL TO STAY AWAY FROM GROUND ZERO ON 9/11 "You've made this easy. Don't show up on 9/11 this year -- or any year. We're not interested in your moral equivalency, nepo baby. Stick to the parlor communism daddy taught you. You and your buddy Piker can spend the day practicing Mandarin," said Fox News contributor and ex-NYPD officer Paul Mauro. "Is this real?," wrote former first lady Jill Biden’s spokesperson Michael La Rosa. "Americans were MURDERED by TERRORISTS in the most horrific way," wrote Rep. Nancy Mace. "What a coward. They were murdered and sleep well at night knowing I and thousands of my brothers did our part to even the f—–g score," wrote "Big Weekend Show" co-host Joey Jones. HASAN PIKER CALLS HAMAS 'FAR MORE MODERATE,' DISMISSES TERROR GROUP’S BRUTAL RULE IN GAZA Mamdani said he plans to attend the 9/11 commemoration to honor the victims, survivors, families and first responders alongside Vice President JD Vance and former presidents including Biden and Bush. A petition organized by several victims’ families called on Mamdani not to participate in the ceremony, with the families questioning whether his participation would be appropriate given the tragedy. "We respectfully ask that the organizers carefully consider whether Mr. Mamdani’s participation would align with the intention of the ceremony and the expectations of the families most directly affected by the tragedy," a Change.org petition organized by several victims' families states.
